He is a member of the [[Galaxy Team]]'s Survey Corps and specializes in {{OBP|Pokémon|species}}'s modes of life. ==In the core series games== ===Pokémon Legends: Arceus=== Professor Laventon finds the {{player}} on [[Jubilife Village|Prelude Beach]] after they have fallen through the [[space-time rift]]. The appearance of the player has attracted the interest of the Professor's three [[first partner Pokémon]]. After the player awakens, the Pokémon run away and the Professor tasks the player with recapturing them. Impressed by their skill he takes the player to [[Jubilife Village]] to recruit them into the [[Galaxy Team]]'s Survey Corps. For most of the game, Professor Laventon can be found at all [[base camp]]s or his laboratory in [[Galaxy Hall]]. The player can report their latest survey results by speaking to Laventon, which entails any Pokémon caught and {{OBP|research task|Legends: Arceus}}s completed since the last report. He will then reward the player with [[Pokémon Dollar|money]] and [[Rank (Galaxy Team)|research points]] based on these results. The [[Pokédex entry|Pokédex entries]] in Pokémon Legends: Arceus are written by Laventon. Incidentally, he coined the term "[[scalchop and seamitar|scalchop]]" for {{p|Oshawott}}'s signature seashell and the term "[[aura]]" for {{p|Lucario}}'s signature energy wave control power. Laventon also observed that {{p|Unown}} resemble human writing from other lands, though no one takes him seriously. ===Pokémon Scarlet and Violet=== Professor Laventon makes a cameo in {{g|Scarlet and Violet}}. During Ms. [[Raifort]]'s history classes, a photo of Laventon appears on the classroom board as part of a timeline on the [[History of Poké Balls|history and development of the Poké Ball]]. ===Pokémon Legends: Z-A=== Professor Laventon makes a cameo in {{g|Legends: Z-A}}, where he is portrayed in an old painting in an office building in [[Lumiose City]]. He is also mentioned several times in the [[Lumiose Museum]]. ===Pokémon=== ====Gives to the player==== Professor Laventon gives the player their choice of [[first partner Pokémon]] from Pokémon he collected while traveling the {{pkmn|world}}. After the player has beaten the main story of Pokémon Legends: Arceus, he will give the player the remaining two first partner Pokémon once spoken to at his lab. {{Pokémon/Grid}} {{Pokémon |gen=LA |ndex=0722 |pokemon=Rowlet |level=5 |gender=both |type1=Grass|type2=Flying |move1=Gust|move1type=Flying|move1cat=Special}} {{Pokémon |gen=LA |ndex=0155 |pokemon=Cyndaquil |level=5 |gender=both |type1=Fire |move1=Quick Attack|move1type=Normal|move1cat=Physical}} {{Pokémon |gen=LA |ndex=0501 |pokemon=Oshawott |level=5 |gender=both |type1=Water |move1=Tackle|move1type=Normal|move1cat=Physical}} {{Pokémon/Grid/end}} ==Gallery== ===Artwork=== {|style="margin:auto; text-align:center; border:3px solid #{{hisui color dark}}; background:#{{hisui color}}; font-size:80%; border-radius: 10px" | style="border:2px solid #{{hisui color light}}; background:#{{hisui color light}}" | [[File:Professor Laventon SV Classroom Board Sprite.png]] |- style="color:#FFF" | Classroom board sprite from the opening of {{color2|FFF|Pokémon Scarlet and Violet|Scarlet and Violet}} |} ==Quotes== {{main|Professor Laventon/Quotes}} ==In the TCG== [[File:ProfessorLaventonSilverTempest162.jpg|200px|thumb|Professor Laventon in the TCG]] {{main|Professor Laventon (Silver Tempest 162)}} '''Professor Laventon''' was introduced as a {{TCG|Supporter card}} in the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]] during the English Sword & Shield Series (the Japanese Sword & Shield Era). It was first released in the Japanese {{TCG|S-P Promotional cards}} and the English {{TCG|Silver Tempest}} expansion, with artwork by [[Ken Sugimori]]. It allows the player to put up to three Pokémon that have "Hisuian" in their names from their discard pile into their hand. {{-}} ==Trivia== * Laventon may draw inspiration from [[wp:William_S._Clark|William S. Clark]], an American zoologist and naturalist whose work initiating the Sapporo Agricultural College was instrumental in modernizing agricultural education and technology in Japan during the Meiji era. Him speaking English in the Japanese version of the game may further allude to this connection. * As the Galaxy Expedition Team consists of foreigners to Hisui, Laventon is the only known [[Pokémon Professor]] in the [[core series]] not to be from the region he resides in. ** In the English translation of the game, there are several hints in the game that Professor Laventon may be from the [[Galar]] region: *** In the [[Pokédex entry]] for {{p|Raichu}}, he mentions {{p|Copperajah}} that live in his homeland, with Galar being the only region where they can be encountered that had been revealed as of the release of the game. *** The writing on the blackboard in his office uses the alphabet from {{g|Sword and Shield}} instead of the style of writing used elsewhere in Pokémon Legends: Arceus. *** He often uses stock British phrases such as "jolly good". In other versions of the game, such as the Japanese and German versions, he will sometimes speak in English instead. * Professor Laventon's drawings that he made for his Pokédex are on display at the [[Lumiose Museum]] in {{g|Legends: Z-A}}.
